reasons: The cited Section 19 meets the preferred position on all material terms: professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel to industry standards (19.1), material conformance to documentation for ninety days after the later of delivery or acceptance for Deliverables and for the full subscription term for Hosted Services (19.2), compliance with Applicable Law and no intentionally introduced malicious code (19.3), and a real remedy of prompt re-perform/repair/replace escalating to termination plus refund of Fees paid (19.4).

The disclaimer in 19.5 is mutual, limited to implied warranties, and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty — no carve-out edit is needed.

The failed deterministic check ('warranty period ≥ 90 days') is a false negative caused by the period being spelled out in words ('ninety days') rather than digits; the substantive period satisfies the preferred 90-day services/deliverable benchmark.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was proposed and no counterparty comment was added; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs.
Only immaterial gaps remain (e.g. 'Fees paid' rather than 'paid or payable'), which the playbook directs to be noted in rationale rather than flagged.
